title: Joseph’s brothers propose death for the cup’s holder and their own enslavement
speaker: Joseph’s brothers
reason: Editor's rewording: the brothers' proposed penalty and self-enslavement, not accepted; context link to ot-genesis-v44-10 (steward's different ruling); cf. AUD-01-31-32.

title: Moses invites Pharaoh to set the time for removing the frogs
speaker: Moses
reason: Moses' imperative 'Appoint a time for me' answers Pharaoh's request (AUD-02-8-4); the catalogue records this exchange's directions and offers nearby.

title: God tells Moses to set the ordinances before Israel
speaker: the Lord
reason: Heading charge ('ordinances which you shall set before them'), recorded like ot-exodus-v19-6 and ot-numbers-v5-12; only broad torah-exodus-21-1 includes it.

title: Bring in and arrange the table and the lampstand
speaker: the Lord
reason: Editor rejected C0275 (no designated sides); as an installation step it gets its own record, like C0368–C0370 for Exodus 40:5–8.

title: Treat a saddle ridden by the man with a discharge as unclean
speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
reason: Reviewed separately as the editor asked: the saddle rule is its own object-impurity law, itemized like C0537–C0538 for vessels.

title: Apply one judgment to resident foreigner and native in the stated penalties
speaker: the Lord through Moses
reason: Editor kept C0114 to its Passover scope; this equal-judgment law closes the penal laws (24:15–21), so it is recorded separately, not combined.

title: Joshua forbids rebuilding Jericho under an oath-curse
speaker: Joshua, by an oath before the Lord
reason: Binding oath-prohibition, recorded like AUD-09-14-24 and AUD-07-21-1. Origin set to Mixed: 1 Kings 16:34 calls it the Lord’s word through Joshua.

additional.context: Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons, “according to the Lord’s word which He spoke through Joshua.”

title: Sisera summons his chariots and army to the Kishon
speaker: Sisera, commander of Jabin’s army
recipient: his nine hundred iron chariots and all his troops
reason: Reported muster order with stated forces and destination, recorded like Jabin’s reported summons (AUD-06-11-1); Sisera’s own order, not a fulfilment.

title: Gideon sounds the trumpet and sends messengers to rally the tribes
speaker: Gideon
recipient: Abiezer; the men of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali
reason: Reported summons to war by trumpet and messengers, answered by the tribes; consistent with recorded musters (AUD-09-11-7, AUD-06-11-1, ot-judges-v7-24).

title: Shechem's men and Maallon's house make Abimelech king at Shechem
speaker: all the men of Shechem and the house of Maallon (Millo)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated king-making with a named appointee, like published AUD-10-2-8 (Abner makes Ish-bosheth king); Jotham's rebuke (AUD-07-9-16) recalls it.

title: Jephthah’s daughter tells her father to fulfil his vow concerning her
speaker: Jephthah’s daughter
reason: A different direction from the mourning request ('do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth'); extending would retitle ot-judges-v11-37.

title: Micah installs one of his sons as priest of his shrine
speaker: Micah
reason: Reported priestly installation (“filled the hand”), an appointment like Jeroboam’s priests (AUD-11-13-33). Topic changed to Sanctuary, priesthood and ministry.

title: Israel arranges a smoke signal with the ambush at Gibeah
speaker: the men of Israel
reason: The prearranged signal is stated in 20:38. Reference narrowed from 20:38–40, since 20:39–40 narrate the battle and the signal’s fulfilment.

title: Saul sounds the trumpet throughout the land to rally Israel
speaker: Saul
reason: Reported call to arms by trumpet and proclamation, answered at Gilgal; distinct from AUD-09-13-2 and consistent with recorded musters such as AUD-09-11-7.

title: Saul tells the priest to withdraw his hand from the inquiry
speaker: King Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Editor: 'Withdraw your hands' is a separate command from bringing the ephod (ot-1-samuel-v14-18); recorded separately as Saul breaks off the inquiry.

title: Saul sentences Abimelech and his father’s house to death
speaker: King Saul
recipient: Abimelech (Ahimelech) the priest and his father’s house
reason: Editor: the sentence addressed to Abimelech is distinct from the guards' order (ot-1-samuel-v22-17); recorded like ot-1-samuel-v14-44, Saul's sentence on Jonathan.

title: David shows Saul the cloak flap and pleads his innocence
speaker: David
reason: Explicit appeal (“Know and see … no evil in my hand”) leaving judgment to the Lord; parallels the recorded plea at 26:19–20. 24:14 remains AUD-09-24-14.

title: The Lord repays with good whoever spares an enemy in distress
speaker: Saul
reason: General maxim teaching mercy to an enemy, recorded as Wisdom like the proverb at AUD-09-24-14; title restated as the saying itself.

title: Nabal’s servant urges Abigail to act before disaster strikes
speaker: one of Nabal’s young men
reason: Explicit urging (“know and see what you will do”), the idiom recorded at Judges 18:14 (AUD-07-18-14); it prompts Abigail’s recorded actions.

title: David sends spies to confirm that Saul has come
speaker: David
reason: Reported reconnaissance commission with a clear task, like David’s reported sending to inquire (AUD-10-11-3) and the catalogue’s spy commissions.

title: The Lord repays each person’s righteousness and faithfulness
speaker: David
reason: General maxim on divine recompense spoken in narrative, recorded as Wisdom like AUD-09-17-45 and AUD-09-24-14.

title: Saul asks the summoned Samuel to tell him what to do
speaker: Saul
recipient: Samuel, brought up by the medium
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit request to a new addressee (“make known to me what I should do”); Saul’s requests to the medium (28:7–13) are recorded nearby.

title: Hadadezer summons the Syrians from beyond the River
speaker: Hadadezer king of Zobah
recipient: the Syrians beyond the River, under Shobach
reason: Reported summons of allied forces, recorded like Jabin’s reported coalition summons (AUD-06-11-1). Link 1 Chronicles 19:16 as its parallel.

additional.context: Chronicles’ parallel: the Syrian sends messengers and brings out the Syrians beyond the River under Sophach.

title: David rules that the rich man in Nathan’s parable must repay sevenfold
speaker: King David
recipient: Nathan, concerning the rich man of the parable
reason: A royal judicial sentence on the case Nathan presents; rulings on staged cases are recorded at 2 Samuel 14:8–11.

title: The Lord sends word through Nathan naming Solomon Jedidiah
speaker: the Lord, through Nathan the prophet
reason: Reported divine naming through a prophet, like AUD-10-12-1 and recorded naming commands (Hosea 1:4). Reference narrowed to 12:25; 12:24 is birth narrative.

title: The woman of Tekoa urges David to bring back his banished son
speaker: the woman of Tekoa, speaking Joab’s words
reason: Her real request behind the staged case, which David treats as a request in 14:21; distinct from her recorded requests at 14:11 and 14:12.

title: Joab finally lets Ahimaaz run after Cushi
speaker: Joab
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Editor: Joab's 'Run' is a separate directive from Ahimaaz's request (ot-2-samuel-v18-22); recorded as the permission answering the earlier refusal (ot-2-samuel-v18-19).

title: Abel’s wise woman pleads with Joab not to destroy the city
speaker: the wise woman of Abel
reason: Plea answered directly by Joab (“Far be it from me … to destroy”); distinct from her summons at 20:16–17, which extending would broaden.

title: David appoints Benaiah to attend him and receive his orders
speaker: King David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported appointment, recorded like AUD-11-2-35 and AUD-09-18-13. Link 1 Chronicles 11:25 (also open as R8a V051) as the parallel.

additional.context: Chronicles’ parallel: David appoints Banaias over his house.

title: Solomon levies Israelite workers for Lebanon and sets overseers over the works
speaker: King Solomon
recipient: the levy from all Israel under Adoniram, and the appointed overseers
reason: Royal labour levy with shifts and appointed overseers, like AUD-13-22-2 and AUD-11-4-7. Link the duplicate notices listed below.

additional.context: The Greek supplement repeats the seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters.
The Greek supplement repeats the three thousand six hundred overseers appointed over Solomon’s works.
Chronicles’ parallel: Solomon gathers the burden-bearers and quarrymen with three thousand six hundred overseers.
Chronicles’ parallel: Solomon counts the resident foreigners and assigns burden bearers, quarrymen and taskmasters.

title: Solomon appoints Jeroboam over the forced labour of Joseph’s house
speaker: King Solomon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported appointment, recorded like AUD-09-18-13 and AUD-11-2-35. Link 1 Kings 12:24b, which retells it.

additional.context: The Greek supplement retells that Solomon made Jeroboam ruler over the burdens of Joseph’s house.

title: The Lord through Ahijah appoints Jeroboam king on condition of obedience
speaker: the Lord, through Ahijah the Shilonite
reason: Divine appointment with a stated covenant charge (keep my commands as David did); distinct from ot-1-kings-v11-31, which records only the torn pieces.

title: Israel rejects David’s house and calls its men to their tents
speaker: the people of Israel (all Israel)
reason: The people’s call to desert David’s house for their tents; same kind as published AUD-10-20-1 (Sheba), but a separate speaker and occasion.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Israel raises the same cry against Rehoboam and goes home.
The Greek supplementary account retells the same cry at Shechem.

title: Israel summons Jeroboam to the assembly and makes him king
speaker: all Israel, in assembly
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated appointment of a king by the assembly, as the catalogue records at AUD-10-2-4 and AUD-10-5-1; no current record.

title: Rehoboam musters Judah and Benjamin to fight the house of Israel
speaker: King Rehoboam
recipient: the assembly of Judah and Benjamin (120,000 warriors)
reason: Reported muster for war, like published AUD-09-13-2 and AUD-09-23-8; countermanded by ot-1-kings-v12-23. Parallels listed as Additional Scripture.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Rehoboam assembles Judah and Benjamin to restore the kingdom by war.
The Greek supplementary account retells Rehoboam gathering Judah and Benjamin to fight Jeroboam.

title: The old prophet tells his sons to saddle his donkey
speaker: the old prophet of Bethel
reason: Direct household order; the catalogue records this kind nearby (AUD-12-4-22, ot-2-kings-v4-24, AUD-11-13-31). Weak, hence low.

title: Israel’s army makes its commander Omri king in the camp
speaker: the people in Israel’s camp at Gibbethon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated king-making by the army, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4 and AUD-10-2-8; 1 Kings 16 has no records.

title: Elijah asks the widow for water and a morsel of bread
speaker: Elijah
reason: Editor: separate requests for water and bread, distinct from the cake request (ot-1-kings-v17-13); recorded separately. 17:12 is the widow's reply, no direction.

title: Elijah tells Baal’s prophets to move away so he can offer
speaker: Elijah the Tishbite
reason: Direct order to Baal’s prophets (‘Move away now’); Elijah’s neighbouring orders at 18:25, 18:27, 18:30 and 18:34 are all recorded.

title: Ben-hadad’s envoys in sackcloth beg Ahab to spare his life
speaker: the son of Ader (Ben-hadad), through his attendants
reason: Ben-hadad’s plea for life to Ahab differs from the proposal to his attendants (ot-1-kings-v21-31); pleas recorded at AUD-12-1-13, ot-1-kings-v1-51.

title: Ahab adjures Micaiah to speak only truth in the Lord’s name
speaker: Ahab king of Israel
reason: An adjuration demanding truth under oath, not a mere rhetorical question; compare ot-1-samuel-v3-17. Chronicles parallel listed.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: the king again puts Micaiah under oath to speak nothing but truth.

title: The army herald sends every man home after Ahab’s death
speaker: the army herald
reason: The herald’s proclaimed dismissal of the army is a new order; it echoes, but does not cite, Micaiah’s word (ot-1-kings-v22-17).

title: Elisha tells the sons of the prophets to keep silent
speaker: Elisha
recipient: the sons of the prophets at Bethel and Jericho
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Elisha’s order ‘Be silent’ is unrecorded. Reference narrowed to 2:3, 5, since 2:4 belongs to AUD-12-2-2.

title: Jehoram asks Jehoshaphat to join his war against Moab
speaker: Jehoram king of Israel
reason: A real request in question form, answered and acted on, like published AUD-09-26-6; the route exchange in 3:8 continues it.

title: Moab’s troops urge one another to plunder the allied camp
speaker: the Moabite troops
reason: Troops urging one another to act, the kind recorded at ot-1-samuel-v4-9; a brief battle cry, hence low.

title: Elisha sends Gehazi to ask the Shunammite what favour she wants
speaker: Elisha
recipient: Gehazi, with a message for the Shunammite woman
reason: Elisha directs Gehazi to deliver an offer of help; distinct from the summons at ot-2-kings-v4-12, and Elisha’s orders nearby are recorded.

title: Elisha sends Gehazi running to ask after the Shunammite’s family
speaker: Elisha
reason: Direct errand order to Gehazi; Elisha’s neighbouring orders to him (4:12, 4:27, 4:29) are recorded.

title: Syria’s king writes Israel’s king to cure Naaman of his leprosy
speaker: the king of Syria, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Editor: the letter conveys a different direction to Israel's king than ot-2-kings-v5-5's sending; recorded as its own royal letter.

title: An attendant advises sending horsemen to scout the abandoned camp
speaker: one of the king of Israel’s attendants
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Counsel to the king, recorded as Instruction as at ot-1-kings-v21-31 and ot-1-kings-v1-2; the king’s resulting commission is ot-2-kings-v7-14.

title: Joram orders his chariot yoked to go and meet Jehu
speaker: Joram king of Israel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Direct order (‘Yoke up!’), carried out; Joram’s and Jehu’s orders in this scene (9:17–19) are recorded.

title: Jehu’s letter dares Samaria’s leaders to crown Ahab’s son and fight
speaker: Jehu, by letter
recipient: the rulers, elders and guardians of Ahab’s sons in Samaria
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Written imperative challenge, like ot-2-kings-v14-8; distinct from the second letter’s order at AUD-12-10-6.

title: Jehoiada crowns and anoints the boy Joash as king
speaker: Jehoiada the priest
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated anointing and coronation, recorded separately from the call to reign (AUD-14-23-3), as with Jehu and Saul. Chronicles parallel listed.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Jehoiada and his sons crown and anoint Joash, and the people acclaim him.

title: Judah’s people make the sixteen-year-old Azariah king
speaker: all the people of Judah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated king-making by the people, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel 2 Chronicles 26:1 is item U11655 elsewhere.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: the people of the land make the sixteen-year-old Uzziah king.

title: Ahaz sends Uriah the Damascus altar’s pattern to copy
speaker: King Ahaz
reason: A building pattern sent for copying, like AUD-13-28-11; 16:11 expressly cites it. Distinct from the sacrifice order at ot-2-kings-v16-15.

title: Hezekiah asks Assyria’s king to withdraw and accepts the imposed tribute
speaker: Hezekiah king of Judah, through messengers
recipient: Sennacherib king of Assyria at Lachish
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit request (‘Withdraw from me’) with submission to tribute; royal appeals like ot-2-kings-v16-7 are recorded. Nothing covers this verse.

title: The Assyrian envoy dares Judah to wager horses with Assyria
speaker: Rhapsakes, the Assyrian envoy
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: The envoy’s imperative taunt is the one unrecorded directive in a speech whose other verses are recorded. Isaiah parallel listed.

additional.context: Isaiah parallel: the envoy’s same dare to join Assyria and match two thousand horses with riders.

title: Hezekiah asks Isaiah for a sign and chooses the shadow’s return
speaker: Hezekiah king of Judah
reason: A request to the prophet, not a prayer, like AUD-11-13-6; Isaiah 38:22 here is a statement, not the request.

title: Manasseh appoints a charmer and spirit-mediums
speaker: King Manasseh
reason: Stated wicked appointment, comparable to AUD-11-13-33 and AUD-02-1-11, though set in a list of sins. Audience corrected to Personal.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Manasseh appoints spirit-mediums and enchanters among his sins.

title: The people of the land make Josiah king after Amon’s murder
speaker: the people of the land
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated king-making by the people of the land, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel listed.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: the people of the land strike Amon’s attackers and make Josiah king.

title: Josiah summons Judah’s elders and reads the covenant book to all
speaker: King Josiah
recipient: the elders of Judah and Jerusalem; all the people
reason: Reported royal summons with public reading, like published AUD-09-22-11; the covenant at 23:3 stays held separately. Chronicles parallel listed.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Josiah gathers the elders and reads the covenant book to all the people.

title: The people of the land anoint Jehoahaz and make him king
speaker: the people of the land
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated anointing and king-making by the people, the kind recorded at AUD-10-2-4. Chronicles parallel 2 Chronicles 36:1 is item U11919 elsewhere.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: the people of the land anoint Jehoahaz and install him as king.

title: Pharaoh Neco makes Eliakim king and renames him Jehoiakim
speaker: Pharaoh Neco (Nechao)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: A foreign king installs and renames a vassal, a stated appointment like AUD-10-2-8. Chronicles 36:4 parallel listed; its tribute clauses belong elsewhere.

additional.context: Chronicles parallel: Pharaoh Neco installs Eliakim as king of Judah and renames him Jehoiakim.

title: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah
speaker: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit appointment of a governor; Gedaliah’s own counsel is recorded (ot-2-kings-v25-24) but not his appointment. Reports listed as Additional Scripture.

additional.context: The commanders hear that Babylon’s king has appointed Gedaliah and come to him.
Jeremiah’s account reports Babylon’s king appointing Gedaliah over the remnant left in the land.

title: David assigns the Levites their offices and divides them into courses
speaker: King David
recipient: the Levites aged thirty and upward
reason: David’s stated assignment of Levitical offices and courses, like AUD-13-24-3; distinct from the duties at ot-1-chronicles-v23-28 (23:28–32).

title: Israel’s twelve army divisions serve the king in monthly turns
speaker: King David’s administration, as reported by the narrator
recipient: the divisions of Israel and their commanders
reason: A monthly service rotation like published AUD-11-4-7; the appointing act is described rather than spoken, hence low. 1 Chronicles 27 has no records.

title: Hiram tells Solomon to bring the rafted timber from Joppa to Jerusalem
speaker: Chiram (Hiram) king of Tyre, by letter
reason: Editor: the timber-transport arrangement is a distinct instruction from Hiram's provisions request (ot-2-chronicles-v2-14); recorded separately. Kings parallel: 1 Kings 5:23.

title: Solomon conscripts the Canaanite remnant but enslaves no Israelite
speaker: King Solomon
recipient: the remaining Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites; Israel
reason: Royal labour policy over conquered peoples, like published AUD-06-9-21 and AUD-13-22-2. Greek parallel 1 Kings 10:22b–22c listed.

additional.context: Kings (Greek) parallel: Solomon subjects the remaining peoples to tribute but puts no Israelite to labour.

title: Solomon rules his Egyptian wife may not live in David’s city
speaker: King Solomon
reason: Quoted royal ruling grounded in the holiness of places the ark entered; 1 Kings 9:9a narrates the move without the ruling.

title: Abijah warns Israel that fighting the Lord will not prosper
speaker: King Abijah
reason: This text states a warning, not an imperative; recorded as Wisdom like AUD-09-25-30 and AUD-09-17-45. Type corrected from Command.

title: Asa’s assembly covenants to seek the Lord on pain of death
speaker: King Asa and the assembly
recipient: Judah, Benjamin and the Israelite settlers living among them
reason: Sworn covenant with a stated obligation and death penalty (15:13), a distinct law; AUD-14-15-1 and AUD-14-14-3 cover other occasions.

title: Hanani rebukes Asa for trusting Syria’s king instead of the Lord
speaker: Hanani (Anani) the prophet
reason: Prophetic rebuke with a maxim on trust (16:9), like AUD-14-15-1. Origin corrected to Earthly: no ‘Thus says the Lord’, as at AUD-14-25-7.

title: Jehoshaphat garrisons Judah’s fortified cities and appoints leaders
speaker: King Jehoshaphat
recipient: his forces and the leaders set over Judah’s and Ephraim’s cities
reason: Stated appointment of leaders and garrisons, like AUD-09-8-1; unnamed appointees and no stated charge, hence low.

title: Jehu orders a search for Ahaziah, who is caught and killed
speaker: Jehu
reason: Reported order of a search, like AUD-09-14-17. The Kings account of Jehu’s order (2 Kings 9:27) is listed as Additional Scripture.

additional.context: Kings account: Jehu pursues the fleeing Ahaziah and orders him struck down too.

title: Hezekiah orders sin offerings on the altar for all Israel
speaker: King Hezekiah
reason: Reported order (29:21) and quoted ruling (29:24). Reference corrected to drop fulfilment narrative 29:22–23.

title: Hezekiah orders the burnt offering, begun with song and trumpets
speaker: King Hezekiah
reason: Reported order to offer the burnt offering, distinct from the instrument arrangement at AUD-14-29-25. Reference corrected: 29:28 is fulfilment narrative.

title: Hezekiah’s assembly decrees a second-month Passover for all Israel
speaker: King Hezekiah, his rulers and the assembly in Jerusalem
recipient: all Israel and Judah, from Beersheba to Dan
reason: Communal decree for a second-month Passover (30:2–5). 30:1, the letters, is linked to ot-2-chronicles-v30-6 instead (E:ot-2-chronicles-v30-6).

title: Hezekiah appoints commanders of war over the people
speaker: King Hezekiah
recipient: the commanders of war over the people
reason: Narrated appointment of war commanders, like AUD-10-18-1; leads into the recorded 32:7 speech. Note: 32:8 completes that speech (extend ot-2-chronicles-v32-7).

title: Josiah stations the priests at their watches and strengthens them
speaker: King Josiah
reason: Narrated assignment of the priests to their courses for Josiah's Passover, parallel in kind to AUD-14-31-2 (Hezekiah); distinct from the Levites' charge (35:3–6).

title: Judah’s rulers make the lament for Josiah an ordinance for Israel
speaker: the male and female rulers of Judah
reason: Stated establishment of an ordinance ('They made it an ordinance for Israel'), consistent with the published lament ordinance AUD-07-11-39 (Judges 11:40).

title: Pharaoh Neco imposes a tribute of silver and gold on Judah
speaker: Pharaoh Neco
reason: Corrected to 36:3, 4a: Neco's stated levy, taxed 'at Pharaoh's command'. 36:4 (Eliakim installed) parallels 2 Kings 23:34; 2 Kings 23:33, 35 parallel this.

additional.context: Kings parallel: Neco imposes the levy of silver and gold on the land.
Kings parallel: Jehoiakim taxes the land to pay it, at Pharaoh's command.

title: Nebuchadnezzar makes Zedekiah king over Judah under an oath by God
speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated king-making with the oath Nebuchadnezzar imposed (36:13), like AUD-10-2-8; 2 Kings 24:17 is the unrecorded parallel.

additional.context: Kings parallel: the king of Babylon makes Mattaniah king and renames him Zedekiah.
Recalls that Nebuchadnezzar made Zedekiah king over Judah.

title: Dying Alexander divides his kingdom among his officers
speaker: Alexander the Macedonian
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Deathbed transfer of rule to his officers, the kind of appointment the catalogue records (AUD-15-6-14, AUD-16-9-23); 1:8 shows its outworking.

title: Antiochus appoints overseers and orders Judah’s cities to sacrifice, city by city
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
recipient: his kingdom; the cities of Judah
reason: New enforcement measures beyond the 1:41–50 decree records: overseers appointed and Judah's cities ordered to sacrifice one by one (cf. 2:15).

title: Antiochus pays his army a year’s wages and orders it ready
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
reason: Reported royal muster and order to the paid army to stand ready; uncovered, and distinct from the Lysias commission (AUD-15-3-32).

title: Judas sends men to spy out Timothy’s camp
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated sending of spies, with their report, as the catalogue records for AUD-06-7-2 and AUD-04-21-32.

title: Judas asks the people of Ephron to let his company pass through
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Request for passage in the same 'We will pass through your land' form the catalogue records at AUD-04-21-21 (Numbers 21:21–22); refused.

title: Judas orders his company to encamp where each man stands
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
reason: Reported order by proclamation with stated content before the assault on Ephron; uncovered, like ot-1-maccabees-v5-42.

title: Lysias makes the young Antiochus king and names him Eupator
speaker: Lysias
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated king-making that sets aside Antiochus's appointment of Philip (AUD-15-6-14); king-makings are recorded (AUD-10-2-8).

title: Judas assembles all the people to besiege the citadel
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
reason: Corrected to 6:19: narrated summons to besiege, like published AUD-09-23-8 (Saul at Keilah); 6:20 is fulfilment narrative.

title: Renegade Israelites petition the king to avenge their brothers
speaker: ungodly men from Israel with escapees from the citadel
reason: Narrower wording as the editor asked: a petition for vengeance and quick action, not an order to attack Judas; cf. ot-1-maccabees-v7-7.

title: Antiochus Eupator breaks his oath and orders Zion’s wall pulled down
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
reason: Reported order with stated content, breaking the sworn terms of 6:60–61; uncovered.

title: Bacchides places the country under Alcimus with a supporting force
speaker: Bacchides
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated handover of the country's government to Alcimus with a force, distinct from his priesthood (AUD-15-7-8); appointments are in scope.

title: Nicanor threatens to burn the temple unless Judas is handed over
speaker: Nicanor
recipient: the priests and elders on Mount Zion
reason: Corrected to 7:35 (7:33–34 narrative): sworn ultimatum demanding Judas be handed over; 2 Maccabees 14:31–33 is the parallel account.

title: Judas sends envoys to Rome to seek alliance and friendship
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: Eupolemus and Jason; the Roman senate
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Judas's embassy to Rome with the envoys' request to the senate (8:20); uncovered. Like AUD-15-12-1; the treaty itself is AUD-15-8-24.

title: Bacchides appoints the ungodly men as masters of the country
speaker: Bacchides
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated appointment by a hostile governor (wicked rulers are in scope); 9:26 shows its outworking. Uncovered.

title: Jonathan sends John to ask the Nabateans to keep their belongings
speaker: Jonathan
recipient: the Nabateans, through his brother John
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported request to the Nabateans carried by his brother (named John in 9:36); typed Command, like AUD-29-44-3.

title: Alcimus orders the wall of the sanctuary’s inner court demolished
speaker: Alcimus
reason: Reported order with stated content against the sanctuary; 9:55 records Alcimus struck down. Uncovered.

title: Bacchides secretly writes to his Judean allies to seize Jonathan
speaker: Bacchides, by letter
reason: Bacchides' own written order to his allies, acting on the lawless men's plot (ot-1-maccabees-v9-58, a different speaker); uncovered.

title: Jonathan sends envoys to Bacchides seeking peace and the captives’ return
speaker: Jonathan
reason: Corrected to 9:70–71: reported request for peace and the captives, granted 'according to his words' under oath; 9:72 is fulfilment narrative.

title: Alexander writes summoning Jonathan to meet him at Ptolemais
speaker: King Alexander, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported written royal summons; the catalogue records summonses (AUD-01-41-14) and the comparable meeting request at ot-1-maccabees-v10-56.

title: Alexander orders Jonathan’s garments removed and him clothed in purple
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported order with stated content, carried out; adding it to ot-1-maccabees-v10-63 (protection order) would change that record's meaning.

title: Demetrius II appoints Apollonius, the governor of Coele-Syria
speaker: Demetrius II
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Stated appointment introducing Apollonius's challenge (ot-1-maccabees-v10-72, Study Context); the office is not named, so the title stays neutral.

title: Jonathan commands his army to stand firm under the cavalry ambush
speaker: Jonathan
reason: Sole witness to Jonathan's order to stand firm ('as Jonathan had commanded'); compare AUD-06-19-49, built on 'at the Lord's command'. Thin.

title: Alexander grants Jonathan a golden clasp and Ekron as an inheritance
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated royal honour and land grant, like AUD-15-10-65 and the grants in AUD-15-11-57; typed Commission to match them. Uncovered.

title: Alexander orders his cities to welcome Ptolemy as his father-in-law
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit reported royal command ('King Alexander had commanded them to meet him'); uncovered.

title: Demetrius II orders Jonathan to lift the siege and come to Ptolemais
speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
reason: Reported written order with stated content, defied in 11:23; uncovered.

title: Jonathan orders the siege of the citadel to continue
speaker: Jonathan
reason: Jonathan's own reported order, defying Demetrius's letter (11:22); a distinct direction, uncovered.

title: Demetrius II confirms Jonathan as high priest and among the First Friends
speaker: King Demetrius II
reason: Narrated royal confirmation in office, like AUD-15-11-57 and AUD-15-10-18; uncovered.

title: Jonathan asks Demetrius II to exempt Judea and the districts from tribute
speaker: Jonathan
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported request; the king consents (11:29) and grants it in ot-1-maccabees-v11-34, a different speaker. Uncovered.

title: Jonathan asks Demetrius II to remove the citadel garrison from Jerusalem
speaker: Jonathan
reason: Reported request with its reason, answered in 11:42–43 (AUD-15-11-42, a different speaker); uncovered.

title: Antiochus VI appoints Simon general from Tyre’s Ladder to Egypt
speaker: the young King Antiochus VI
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Separate appointment of Simon; adding it to AUD-15-11-57 (Jonathan's confirmation) would change that record's meaning.

title: Rome gives Jonathan’s envoys letters ordering their safe escort home
speaker: the Roman council
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Corrected to 12:4: Roman safe-conduct letters to local authorities. 12:3 is the envoys' delivery of Jonathan's commission (extended to AUD-15-12-1 under N:GAP-15-12-16).

title: Areus of Sparta asks Onias to write and declares their goods shared
speaker: Areus king of the Spartans, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Royal letter with a request (12:22) and a command (12:23); uncovered. 12:7–8 expressly recall it and could be linked as Additional Scripture.

title: Tryphon sends forces to destroy all Jonathan’s men in Galilee
speaker: Tryphon
reason: Reported sending of forces with a stated mission, like published AUD-15-16-17; uncovered.

title: Simon sends Jonathan son of Absalom with a force to Joppa
speaker: Simon
reason: Reported military commission (sent with a force; Joppa taken); uncovered, like ot-1-maccabees-v5-17.

title: The citadel garrison urges Tryphon to come through the wilderness with food
speaker: those in the citadel
reason: Reported request carried by envoys; Tryphon acts on it (13:22). Uncovered.

title: Simon sends envoys to Demetrius II to seek remission for the country
speaker: Simon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported embassy with a stated request; Demetrius's reply is AUD-15-13-36, a different speaker. Uncovered.

title: Arsaces sends a commander to capture Demetrius alive
speaker: Arsaces king of Persia and Media
reason: Reported commission with a stated mission (seize Demetrius alive); 14:3 is fulfilment. Typed Commission, like AUD-15-16-17.

title: Sparta resolves to honour the Jewish envoys and record their words
speaker: the people of Sparta, by resolution
recipient: the Spartans; reported by letter to Simon and the Jews
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Corrected to 14:22–23: the Spartan people's resolution with stated actions; 14:20–21 are greeting and report. Foreign civic decree, hence low.

title: Jeremiah orders the deportees to take some of the altar fire
speaker: Jeremiah the prophet, as found in the records
reason: Distinct reported order (take the fire); adding it to AUD-16-2-2 (remember the law) would change that record. 1:19 narrates its fulfilment.

title: Heliodorus’s companions beg Onias to pray for his life
speaker: some of Heliodorus’s companions
reason: Reported request to the high priest to intercede, like AUD-29-44-3; Onias acts on it (3:32). Uncovered.

title: Jason’s envoys ask that his money for Heracles not fund sacrifice
speaker: the envoys Jason sent to Tyre
recipient: those receiving the gift at Tyre
reason: Corrected to 4:19: the bearers' reported request with its reason (unfitting); 4:20 is outcome narrative. Uncovered.

title: Antiochus gives Menelaus, Jason’s envoy, the high priesthood by royal orders
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
reason: Royal grant of the high priesthood by 'royal orders' (4:25); 4:23 introduces Menelaus as Jason's envoy. Speaker narrowed to the king.

title: Antiochus summons Menelaus and Sostratus over the unpaid royal funds
speaker: King Antiochus (Epiphanes)
recipient: Menelaus the high priest and Sostratus, commander of the citadel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported royal summons after Sostratus demanded the unpaid funds; the catalogue records reported summons (AUD-31-5-9, AUD-01-41-14). 4:27 completes the sentence.

title: The council of elders sends three men to accuse Menelaus
speaker: the council of elders
reason: Narrated commission of three delegates to present the case against Menelaus; envoy sendings are recorded (AUD-15-12-1), but this one is incidental.

title: Antiochus leaves Philip and Andronicus as overseers to afflict the people
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
recipient: Philip in Jerusalem and Andronicus at Gerizim, with Menelaus
reason: Narrated appointment of hostile overseers, like published AUD-15-3-32 and AUD-16-5-24; no current record covers it.

title: Apollonius orders his troops to parade under arms on the Sabbath
speaker: Apollonius, commander of the Mysians
reason: Reported order by Apollonius exploiting the Sabbath rest, distinct from the king’s commission (AUD-16-5-24); 5:26 shows the ruse’s purpose.

title: Antiochus compels seven brothers and their mother to eat forbidden pork
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes and his torturers
recipient: the seven brothers and their mother
reason: Reported hostile compulsion: the king forces the brothers to eat pork (7:1), restated in the torturers’ demand (7:7); reference widened to include 7:1.

title: Facing death at human hands, look to God’s hope of resurrection
speaker: the fourth brother, as he was dying
reason: A ‘preferable’ saying on facing death with hope in God; the judgment on the king is context. Compare AUD-16-9-11’s ‘it is right’ saying.

title: Judas appoints his brothers over four divisions with the watchword “God’s help”
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: Simon, Joseph, Jonathan and Eleazar, over the army’s divisions
reason: Narrated appointments of division commanders and a watchword before battle, like AUD-15-13-53; the public reading is context. Draft title reworded.

title: Antiochus orders his charioteer to drive on without stopping toward Jerusalem
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
reason: Reported royal order, renewed in 9:7 (‘ordering the journey hastened’); his boast is context. Reference adds 9:7.

title: Antiochus Eupator appoints Lysias chief minister and governor of Coele-Syria
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated royal appointment, like published AUD-15-10-65; distinct from Antiochus IV’s regency charge to Lysias (AUD-15-3-32).

title: Maccabeus leaves Simon, Joseph and Zacchaeus to besiege the two towers
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: Simon, Joseph and Zacchaeus with their men
reason: Narrated assignment of a besieging force, like published AUD-15-4-41; the bribery and executions that follow are narrative.

title: Judas urges his men to share the danger and help their brothers
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
reason: Reported battle exhortation on a new occasion (Beth-zur), as the catalogue records Judas’s others (AUD-16-8-16, AUD-16-13-14).

title: Lysias urges the Jews to settle on every just condition
speaker: Lysias, the king’s guardian and chief minister
reason: Lysias's message urging settlement (11:14) is the direction; 11:13 and 11:15 narrate, and 11:16–21 is a letter of report and conditional promise (independent check).

title: Roman envoys tell the Jews to send word quickly on referred matters
speaker: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, Roman envoys, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit requests by letter (‘send someone immediately… hurry and send some men’); no record covers the Roman letter.

title: Joppa’s common decree lures its Jews aboard boats to be drowned
speaker: the people of Joppa, by common decree
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
reason: A civic decree carried out as a treacherous invitation; hostile decrees are recorded as such (cf. ot-2-maccabees-v6-8).

title: The defeated Arabs ask Judas for pledges of peace
speaker: the defeated Arab nomads
reason: Reported request for peace pledges, granted in 12:12; such petitions are recorded nearby (ot-1-maccabees-v11-50).

title: Judas’s men urge the Scythopolitans to remain favourable to the Jews
speaker: Judas and his men
reason: Reported request for continued goodwill, like recorded loyalty requests (AUD-16-9-26); borderline courtesy, so low confidence.

title: Judas collects silver and sends it to Jerusalem for a sin offering
speaker: Judas Maccabeus, commended by the narrator
recipient: his men and the priests in Jerusalem
reason: Judas’s levy and sending of silver for a sin offering, kept separate from AUD-16-12-40 per its note; the narrator’s commendation is context.

title: Antiochus Eupator orders Menelaus taken to Beroea and put to death
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator, at Lysias’s prompting
reason: Explicit reported execution order; 13:5–8 describe the local custom and its justice and stay as context.

title: Judas posts armed men at strategic places against treachery
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
reason: Narrated posting of armed guards before the conference, like published AUD-15-12-26 (Jonathan’s armed watch).

title: Nicanor urges Judas to marry and have children
speaker: Nicanor
reason: Reported personal urging, at once complied with; a direction to Judas not covered elsewhere.

title: Nicanor orders the priests to hand over Judas, threatening the temple
speaker: Nicanor
reason: Reported order (14:31) and sworn demand (14:33) to hand over Judas, in scope; parallel 1 Maccabees 7:33–35 pending in R2a (GAP-15-7-33).

title: Nicanor sends five hundred soldiers to arrest the elder Razis
speaker: Nicanor
reason: Reported sending of troops to arrest Razis, a hostile order like AUD-16-5-11; 14:40 states its purpose.

title: Nicanor commands arms taken up on the Sabbath for the king’s business
speaker: Nicanor
recipient: his army, including the Jews compelled to accompany him
reason: Nicanor’s explicit counter-command answering 15:2–4; a hostile order distinct from the Jews’ recorded plea (ot-2-maccabees-v15-2).

title: Judas orders Nicanor’s head and hand displayed and his tongue cut up
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: his men and the countrymen gathered at Jerusalem
reason: Explicit reported orders (15:30, 15:33) with summons (15:31); 1 Maccabees 7:47 narrates the same display and could be linked.

title: The returned leaders set the Levites over the temple building work
speaker: Zorobabel, Iesous and the returned priests and Levites
recipient: the Levites from twenty years old and upward
reason: Narrated appointment of Levites over the rebuilding, like published AUD-14-31-2; Ezra 3 has no record.

title: Officials’ letter asks Artaxerxes to search the records about Jerusalem
speaker: Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and their colleagues, by letter
reason: Petition by letter; title narrowed to the stated request for a search, since halting the work is implied, not asked.

title: Thanthanai asks Darius to search the archives and send word
speaker: Thanthanai the governor, Satharbouzana and their colleagues, by letter
reason: Explicit petition to the king to search the archives and reply; no record covers the letter’s request.

title: Darius decrees a search of the royal archives in Babylon
speaker: Darius the king
reason: Royal decree granting the 5:17 request, like AUD-19-6-1 (records searched by royal order); the scroll found is context.

title: The returned exiles station priests and Levites in divisions for temple service
speaker: the sons of Israel returned from the deportation
reason: Narrated appointment of priestly and Levitical divisions, like AUD-14-23-18 and AUD-14-31-2; grounded in Moses’ book, hence mixed origins.

title: Ezra and family heads are set apart to examine the foreign marriages
speaker: the returned community (the sons of the deportation)
recipient: Ezra the priest and the heads of ancestral houses
reason: Appointment of examiners implementing the assembly’s proposal (ot-ezra-v10-14), as AUD-15-4-42 follows ot-1-maccabees-v4-36.

title: Gatekeepers, singers and Levites are appointed once the wall is built
speaker: Nehemiah, reporting the appointments
reason: Narrated appointment of temple personnel, like AUD-18-12-44; distinct from the gate orders that follow (ot-nehemiah-v7-3).

title: The people cast lots to settle one in ten in Jerusalem
speaker: the people of Judah and their rulers
recipient: the families of Judah living in the towns
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Communal resettlement by lot, comparable to the lot arrangement recorded as Law at Nehemiah 10:35; attributed to the people.

title: Levites are sought out and brought to Jerusalem for the wall’s dedication
speaker: the leaders at Jerusalem (unnamed in the text)
reason: Narrated summons of the Levites to celebrate, as the catalogue records summons (AUD-10-15-12); the dedication rite has no record.

title: Nehemiah stations two great thanksgiving choirs on the wall
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the rulers of Judah and two companies of singers
reason: Nehemiah’s narrated stationing of the thanksgiving choirs, like AUD-14-29-25; 12:32–42 describe the procession.

title: Nehemiah establishes service divisions for priests and Levites and the wood offering
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the priests, Levites and wood carriers
reason: Nehemiah’s closing arrangement of service divisions and the wood offering, echoing 10:35; the prayers in 13:29 and 13:31 are out of scope.

title: The king orders the stewards to follow his and the guests’ wishes
speaker: King Artaxerxes
recipient: the stewards of the royal household
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported royal order governing the feast, in the scene of AUD-19-1-10; the narrator’s note on established law is context.

title: The king orders Mordecai’s loyalty recorded as a memorial in the library
speaker: King Artaxerxes
recipient: the keepers of the royal records (unnamed)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported royal order; the memorial is read back in 6:1–2 (AUD-19-6-1). Not covered elsewhere.

title: Esther sends Achrathaeus to learn from Mordecai what has happened
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Narrated sending of a messenger with a charge, like ot-esther-v4-10 later in the same exchange.

title: Esther invites the king and Haman to her reception today
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Esther’s request answering the king’s ‘what is your petition?’ (5:3); her petitions are recorded nearby (AUD-19-7-3, AUD-19-8-3).

title: The king orders Haman brought quickly to Esther’s reception
speaker: King Artaxerxes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit royal summons, like ot-esther-v6-5.

title: Esther asks the king and Haman to come again tomorrow
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Her second request, framed as ‘my request and my petition’, made on a new occasion (the first reception).

title: The king permits a second day and orders Haman’s sons hanged
speaker: King Artaxerxes
reason: Royal order granting Esther’s recorded request (ot-esther-v9-13); a new direction from the king to the Jews of Susa.

title: Let the righteous resist the lawless and the faithful hold their way
speaker: Job
recipient: his friends, concerning the righteous and faithful
reason: Jussive exhortation that the righteous persevere and resist the lawless; wisdom on conduct, not a prayer or curse. Title adds 17:8.

title: Job did not withhold help from the poor, widow, orphan or naked
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
reason: Oath clause on care for the needy with its motive (31:23); Job 31’s other clauses are published as Wisdom (AUD-20-31-1, AUD-20-31-13).

title: Job disowns trust in wealth and secret homage as lying to God
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
reason: Oath clause on trusting wealth and secret homage, judged lawlessness before God (31:28); title follows the Saints wording rather than sun-worship.

title: Job kept his door open and lodged every stranger
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
reason: Oath clause on hospitality to strangers, recorded like Job 31’s other published clauses (AUD-20-31-1, AUD-20-31-13).

title: Job tore up debtors’ bonds, taking nothing from the debtor
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
reason: Oath clause in the Greek text: fearing the Lord, he returned written bonds and exacted nothing; 31:35a’s plea is context.

title: Others urge the psalmist to flee to the mountains like a bird
speaker: unnamed counsellors quoted by the psalmist
reason: Explicitly quoted counsel the psalmist rejects; the catalogue records such quoted speech in Psalms (AUD-21-70-10) and rejected counsel (ot-job-v2-9e).

title: Love of pleasure, wine and oil marks the needy man
speaker: Proverbial teacher (Solomon's proverbs)
reason: Only unrecorded proverb in chapter 21, where every saying is a Wisdom record. Title follows the Saints wording (the needy man loves pleasure).

title: The bloodthirsty hate the holy, but the upright care for his life
speaker: Proverbial teacher (Solomon's proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men)
reason: Only unrecorded proverb in chapter 29 apart from linked 29:17; a contrastive saying like its neighbours. Title glosses 'seek his life' as care.

title: Like the leech’s daughters, Hades, desire and fire never say ‘Enough’
speaker: Agur, the man who speaks to those who trust in God
reason: Numerical saying on insatiable things, of the same kind as recorded 30:18–31; teaches the restlessness of desire. Title revised to the Saints list.

title: Oppression without a comforter makes the unborn more fortunate
speaker: Ecclesiastes (Qoheleth, the Teacher)
reason: Qoheleth's verdict on oppression, like published observations AUD-23-6-3 and AUD-23-8-9; the only unrecorded passage in chapter 4.

title: Sirach’s sayings on a wife supporting her husband and an evil wife
speaker: Ben Sira
reason: Sayings on a wife's upkeep, an evil wife and sin's beginning, the kind published nearby (AUD-27-25-16, -19). Title revised to the Saints wording.

title: Woe to the lawless, whose own works will come back on them
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
reason: Divine woe on the lawless, like published Isaiah woes (AUD-28-5-8, AUD-28-10-1); 3:10's plot (ot-isaiah-v3-10) is the speech it condemns.

title: Moab’s devourers are told to trample its vineyards as far as Iazer
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Moab)
recipient: the devourers of nations (invaders of Moab)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit summons to attackers, like recorded Jeremiah 5:10; low because the surrounding Greek-based lines are obscure.

title: The watchman tells the inquirer from Seir to seek and stay near
speaker: the watchman in Isaiah’s vision
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: The watchman’s reply to the recorded call of 21:11 adds his own direction (‘seek, and dwell beside me’); different speaker, so not an extension.

title: The ships of Carthage are told to wail over Tyre’s fall
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle concerning Tyre)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Oracle imperatives (an inclusio at 23:1 and 23:14) to Carthage's ships; the catalogue records the parallel 23:6 and 23:10 imperatives.

title: The earth’s people are told to wail over the vanished wine
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit wail summons in the world-judgment oracle, of the kind published at Isaiah 13:6 and 15:2; addressee is the earth’s inhabitants (24:6).

title: Hope belongs to the devout; woe to those who reject the law
speaker: voices from the ends of the earth (Isaiah’s oracle)
reason: Woe-saying naming a sin, like the published Isaiah woes (AUD-28-5-8); low because it is reported, future speech in the oracle.

title: The message is to be announced to Jacob and proclaimed in Judah
speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Explicit summons to proclaim, like published AUD-29-4-16 and AUD-29-31-4; it introduces the Study Context address of 5:21.

title: Egypt’s routed troops urge one another to flee home
speaker: Egypt’s soldiers (quoted in the oracle)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Quoted mutual exhortation (‘Let us rise and return’), the kind recorded at Jeremiah 28:9–10 and 6:4–5.

title: The officials agree to report all the scroll’s words to the king
speaker: the officials (rulers) of Judah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Mutual resolution (‘Let us… report’), like recorded 2 Kings 7:9; a different direction from the summons in AUD-29-43-14, so not an extension.

title: Jerusalem is told to bear her shame for outdoing her sisters
speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
reason: Explicit imperatives to Jerusalem (‘receive your torment… be ashamed’), comparable to recorded Ezekiel 36:32; a distinct oracle, so a separate record.

title: The king hands Daniel over to destruction under the crowd’s pressure
speaker: the king of Babylon
recipient: his companions, before the hostile crowd
reason: Royal sentence handing Daniel to death, like the recorded order of Darius (AUD-31-6-15); spoken to his companions under the crowd's pressure.

title: Israel’s love of its Bethel and Gilgal rites is to be announced
speaker: the Lord through Amos
reason: Explicit summons to proclaim Israel’s guilt, like recorded Amos 3:9 and 3:13; low because the addressee is unnamed and the tone indicting.

title: The devil demands Jesus make bread, leap down and worship him
speaker: the devil (the tempter)
reason: Solicitations to sin are recorded (Potiphar’s wife AUD-01-39-7, Job 2:9). Origin is non-divine. Link Luke 4:3, 5–7, 9–11 as Additional Scripture.

title: The returning unclean spirit warns of a worse end for this generation
speaker: Jesus
recipient: the scribes and Pharisees seeking a sign
reason: Distinct warning parable closing the sign discourse; the editor kept it out of AUD-44-12-22. Link Luke 11:24–26 as Additional Scripture.

title: Jesus grants the Canaanite woman’s plea: let it happen as you wish
speaker: Jesus
recipient: a Canaanite woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon
reason: Unrecorded episode; healing grant like AUD-44-8-13 and AUD-44-9-28, with the disciples’ request ‘Dismiss her’. Link Mark 7:24–30 (‘go’, 7:29).

title: Know the Scriptures and God’s power: He is God of the living
speaker: Jesus
recipient: the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection
reason: Jesus’ answer is unrecorded (only the Sadducees’ question links to S156); controversy teaching is recorded as Wisdom, e.g. AUD-47-5-36. Link Mark 12:24–27; Luke 20:34–38.

title: The high priest adjures Jesus; the council rules him liable to death
speaker: Caiaphas the high priest and the council
reason: Explicit adjuration (26:63) and the council’s verdict (26:66); trial rulings are recorded nearby (AUD-47-18-28, AUD-47-19-6). Link Mark 14:55–64; Luke 22:66–71.

title: Pilate disclaims the blood and hands Jesus over to be crucified
speaker: Pilate the governor
recipient: the crowd, and the soldiers who carry out the crucifixion
reason: Reported sentence, like recorded rulers’ orders (AUD-44-2-16, AUD-44-14-9); type changed to Command. Link Mark 15:15; Luke 23:24–25; John 19:16.

title: Gabriel forbids John wine and strong drink and foretells his Elijah mission
speaker: the angel Gabriel
reason: Not the naming order: 1:15–17 sets John’s abstention and Elijah mission, recorded like AUD-07-13-5 (Judges 13:5). 1:14 is prediction. 1:17 recalls AUD-43-3-22.

title: The great supper warns invited guests against making excuses
speaker: Jesus
recipient: A fellow guest at a Pharisee leader’s table, with the other guests
reason: Luke’s great supper is a distinct parable; AUD-44-22-1’s note distinguishes it, and the catalogue records talents and minas separately. Includes 14:24.

title: Believe all that the prophets spoke about the Christ’s suffering
speaker: the risen Jesus
recipient: two disciples on the road to Emmaus
topic: Minor Teachings: The Scriptures Read in Christ
reason: Unrecorded rebuke for not believing the prophets, with Jesus’ own exposition; distinct from AUD-46-24-5 (remember his words) and K094. Audience set to General.

title: Jesus gives Simon the name Cephas, that is, Peter
speaker: Jesus
topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
reason: Naming decree; divine renamings are itemized (C0034, C0058), and Mark 3:16 and Matthew 16:18 sit inside other records. Andrew’s testimony (1:41) is the occasion.

title: He must increase, but I must decrease
speaker: John the Baptist
reason: John’s maxim that all is given from heaven and his self-effacement teach humility in service; no record covers John 3:22–36.

title: Caiaphas counsels that one man should die for the people
speaker: Caiaphas the high priest
recipient: the council of chief priests and Pharisees
reason: Counsel directing the council’s course, adopted in 11:53 and recalled at John 18:14 (link it); like AUD-48-5-34. Type changed from Wisdom to Instruction.

title: Pilate finds no charge and invokes the Passover custom of release
speaker: Pilate
reason: Pilate states his finding and the Passover release custom (cf. AUD-47-18-28). Another reviewer judged the Mark parallel an offer and custom, not a direction: editor's call.

title: Sergius Paulus summons Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God
speaker: Sergius Paulus, proconsul of Cyprus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Reported official summons, recorded as the catalogue records Acts 20:17, Acts 22:30 and Genesis 41:14; distinct from the 13:14–16 invitation.

title: Festus convenes his tribunal at Caesarea and orders Paul brought in
speaker: Festus
recipient: The officers holding Paul at Caesarea
reason: Editor kept AUD-48-25-4 to 25:4–5; the 25:6 order, retold at 25:17, is recordable like AUD-48-22-30. 25:17 as Additional Scripture.

title: Make it your aim to please the Lord before Christ’s judgment seat
speaker: Paul
reason: Distinct teaching after 5:1–8: aim to please the Lord, since all must appear before Christ’s judgment seat; first-person teaching is recorded as Wisdom (AUD-51-4-16).

title: Wage spiritual warfare, taking every thought captive to obey Christ
speaker: Paul
topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
reason: Paul’s appeal (10:1–2) and teaching on non-fleshly warfare (10:3–5) are unrecorded; AUD-51-10-7 carries a different direction from 10:7.

title: Know how one ought to conduct oneself in God’s household, the church
speaker: Paul
recipient: Timothy, for the church at Ephesus
reason: States the norm the church-order directions serve: how one ought to conduct oneself in God’s household, the church. Audience set to General.

title: Abraham, Sarah, Isaac and Jacob as examples of faith
speaker: the author of Hebrews
topic: Minor Teachings: The Scriptures Read in Christ
reason: Same kind as A072 and A073; 11:13–16 teaches living as sojourners seeking a heavenly homeland. Topic matched to A072/A073. 11:8, 17–19 links stay.

title: Israel, Rahab, the judges, prophets and martyrs as examples of faith
speaker: the author of Hebrews
topic: Minor Teachings: The Scriptures Read in Christ
reason: Examples of faith after A073. 11:28–30 recall recorded directions and are linked to C0095, C0121 and ot-joshua-v6-8 instead (independent check).

title: The living creatures call ‘Come’ as each of four horsemen rides out
speaker: the four living creatures
reason: The four living creatures' 'Come' at each seal; trimmed to the four calls so it does not overlap AUD-70-6-5 (6:6).
